title: Houses of worship protected
hook: permission to defend is given, for otherwise monasteries, churches, synagogues and mosques would be pulled down (22:39–40)

segments.voice: Yesterday, blind hearts, and your line was hearts see. What did you notice on a route you'd stopped looking at? Day four hundred eighty-eight.

For thirteen years in Mecca, the early Muslims were mocked, boycotted, beaten, and some were killed. Through all of it, they were told to be patient and not to strike back. Then most of them left their homes and went north to Medina. And around that time, according to many commentators, came the first verses that gave permission to fight back. What's striking is the reason the verses give. It isn't only, you've been wronged. It's a list of buildings.
screen: `THE REASON IS A LIST OF BUILDINGS.`

segments.voice: Verse thirty-nine says permission is given to those who are fought against, because they have been wronged. Verse forty describes them: people driven from their homes unjustly, only because they said, our Lord is God. And then it explains why such permission exists at all. If God did not check some people by means of others, Pickthall says, "cloisters and churches and oratories and mosques, wherein the name of Allah is oft mentioned, would assuredly have been pulled down." Four kinds of building, in Arabic: sawami', biya', salawat, masajid. Commentators explain them roughly this way: sawami' are the retreats of monks and hermits; biya' are churches; salawat, many say, are the prayer houses of the Jews; and masajid are mosques. The mosque comes last in the list. And the phrase, where the name of God is often remembered, sits over all four. Commentators differ on whether it belongs to the mosques alone or to every house in the list, and many take it the wider way. That's a remarkable thing to find in the very verse that first allows a persecuted community to defend itself. The reason given isn't only to protect our own. It's that without some check on oppression, places of prayer of every kind come down. History offers plenty of examples where that ideal was broken, by people of many faiths. The verse still stands as a measure. A defense that pulls down a church or a synagogue has forgotten the reason it was permitted in the first place.
screen: `DRIVEN OUT FOR SAYING: OUR LORD IS GOD.` · `CLOISTERS, CHURCHES, ORATORIES, MOSQUES.` · `THE MOSQUE COMES LAST IN THE LIST.` · `THE REASON IS THE MEASURE.`

segments.voice: Here's the practice: hold every house of prayer in mind. Sit, and let the breath settle. Picture the places of worship near where you live. A mosque, a church, a synagogue, a temple, a gurdwara, a small room where people meet to pray. Picture them on a Friday, a Saturday, a Sunday, full of people. If you pray, you can ask for their protection, all of them. If you don't, simply wish them safety. The bell holds the time.
Houses of worship protected. In Surah Al-Hajj, the reason for self-defense includes cloisters, churches, oratories and mosques, where God's name is remembered. Today's word.
Your line: all houses of prayer protected. Today, when you pass a place of worship that isn't yours, slow down for a second and wish it well. Day four hundred eighty-eight.

howItsDone: Muslim scholars and community leaders often cite 22:40 when speaking about the protection of places of worship, including after attacks on churches, synagogues, temples and mosques.

fork.setup: a community driven from its homes is finally given permission to defend itself. what reason does the verse give?
options: to take back what was lost, and more.
so that houses of prayer of every kind aren't pulled down.
so that the community can grow larger.
fork.reveal: the verse gives a list: cloisters, churches, oratories and mosques. the reason is the protection of worship itself.

original.note: Arabic: prayers; in 22:40 many commentators read it as the prayer houses of the Jews.

trapdoor: what you thought: a verse about permission to fight.
what it means: the permission comes with a reason: without some check on oppression, places of prayer of every kind would be destroyed.
what a scholar hears: sawami', biya', salawat, masajid; commentators differ on whether 'where God's name is oft mentioned' qualifies only the masajid or all four.

notes: Pickthall wording of the 22:40 phrase quoted from memory; please confirm exactly.
The meanings of sawami', biya', salawat and masajid follow common tafsir explanations; confirm, especially salawat as Jewish places of prayer.
'Many commentators' place 22:39 as the first permission to fight; confirm.
The scope of 'where the name of Allah is oft mentioned' (all four or masajid only) is a real tafsir debate; confirm 'many take it the wider way'.
The sentence about history breaking the ideal 'by people of many faiths' is deliberately general; confirm it is fair.
Thirteen years in Mecca is the standard count; confirm.
